passages.original: Igitur, ut diximus, in ipso primo Jordanis egressu, Phaniada civitas a sita cet, in qua habetur statua ex electro purissimo fabricata, in qua Redemptoris no. stri forma dicitur esse expressa. Nam, ut a plerisque audivi, qui eam contemplati fuerant, mira claritas in ejus facie continetur. Sed ne cui videatur absurdum, narrare quae de ea Cæsariensis refert Eusebius non pigebit. Ait enim : c Mulierein quam sanguinis profluvio laborantem a Salvatore curatam Evangelia tradiderunt, bujus urbis civem constat fuisse, domusque ejus in ea etiam nunc ostenditur. Pro foribus vero domus ipsius, basis quaedam in loco editiore collocata monstratur, in qua mulieris 744 ipsius velut genibus provolutae, palmasque suppliciter tendentis, imago aerea videtur expressa.
passages.english: So, as we have said, at the very first outflow of the Jordan lies the city of Paneas, in which there is a statue made of the purest electrum, in which the form of our Redeemer is said to be represented. For, as I have heard from many who had looked upon it, a wonderful brightness is contained in its face. But so that this may not seem absurd to anyone, it will not be tiresome to relate what Eusebius of Caesarea reports about it. For he says: "It is agreed that the woman whom the Gospels record as suffering from a flow of blood and cured by the Saviour was a citizen of this city, and her house is still shown in it even now. And before the doors of that house a certain base is shown, set in a raised place, on which a bronze image of the woman herself appears to be represented, as if fallen on her knees and stretching out her palms in supplication.
passages.notes: "Phaniada" is taken as Paneas (Caesarea Philippi). "a sita cet" is read as "sita est"; the stray "a" and "c" before "Mulierem" are taken as footnote marks. "744" is a page number and is omitted. "Electrum" may mean either the gold-silver alloy or a fine bronze; Eusebius's account that follows speaks of bronze.
